identity.name: Zhili clique
alt_names: Cao Kun and Wu Peifu's regime

successors.note: The split with the Guominjun (Chahar, Suiyuan, Beijing) is not on the pages.

'It was named for Zhili Province (modern-day Hebei), which was the clique's base of power', plus Beijing, the seat of the central government; Zhili and Fengtian entered Nanyuan for the takeover of Beijing on 23 July 1920. No infobox area.

correction.text: Zhili, Rehe, Chahar, Suiyuan, Henan, Jiangsu, Jiangxi and Hubei, 1922-1923

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: after the 1922 victory the clique 'took control of Rehe (Jehol), Chahar, and Suiyuan and consolidated its control over Henan'; 'At its height, it also controlled Jiangsu, Jiangxi, and Hubei' (undated on the Zhili page; confidence 1 in the ledger).

New keyframe, the high point: Fujian 'gained' by Sun Chuanfang in March 1924, and Zhejiang and Shanghai after the Jiangsu-Zhejiang War of 3 September - 12 October 1924. The north (Zhili, Rehe, Chahar, Suiyuan) is lost in November 1924, so the year shows both; the 1925 shape follows. correction.text: Wu Peifu's and Sun Chuanfang's provinces, 1925-1926

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the 1926 snapshot of the Northern Expedition page: 'Wu Peifu: Held northern Hunan, Hubei, and Henan in 1926'; 'Sun Chuanfang: Held Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Anhui, and Jiangxi in 1926'. Taken for 1925-1926 (the pages give no 1925 snapshot; Sun's Anhui is the researcher's reading of the page). [ea-08-x repair 2026-10-25: the shape is the year-end one. Jiangsu and Anhui were Fengtian's from August to November 1925 (ledger events 1925-8 and 1925-11), so they are in this shape only from the late-1925 return of Sun Chuanfang.]

New keyframe: only Sun Chuanfang's Jiangsu and Anhui remain after Zhejiang (by 23 February 1927) and Shanghai (22 March 1927) fall; Sun was beaten at Longtan in late August 1927. Henan left with the Guominjun's capture of Luoyang on 28 May 1927 (loss event 1927-5, Northern Expedition page).

region.text: Zhili Province with Beijing and Tianjin

ledger.note: 1920: the Zhili clique wins the capital. Zhili-Anhui War, 'July 14, 1920 - July 23, 1920', 'Zhili and Fengtian victory'; Duan Qirui resigned on 19 July and 'On July 23 the combined Fengtian and Zhili cliques entered Nanyuan for the takeover of Beijing'. The Zhili page: 'Active: 1920-1928'; the clique had formed earlier from officers 'snubbed by Premier Duan Qirui' (undated).

1922 (bridging): the Zhili page says only that the clique 'consolidated its control over Henan' and 'At its height, it also controlled Jiangsu, Jiangxi, and Hubei', with no dates; the year is the researcher's reading of the 1922 victory.
April 1922: the First Zhili-Fengtian War. Infobox 'April 10, 1922 - June 18, 1922'; 'Zhili declared war on April 25, 1922, and fighting began on April 29'.

18 June 1922: Zhili victory; the peace was signed aboard a British warship off Qinhuangdao; 'Shanhaiguan subsequently became the border between the two cliques'; Wu Peifu's armies 'took control of the central government in Beijing'.

1922: Rehe, Chahar and Suiyuan come under Zhili control. Zhili 'gained control over Rehe (Jehol), Chahar, and Suiyuan' and 'consolidated control in Henan' after the war. The pages do not say whom they were taken from: they were Beiyang special districts.

By the summer of 1924 (bridging): the Anhui clique page says 'all their provinces were eventually annexed by the Zhili clique by the summer of 1924' (re-read 2026-10-25) and dates only Fujian (March 1924) and Zhejiang and Shanghai (12 October 1924); Anhui province itself is not named as lost, so the year is the page's and the province is the clique's namesake, a reading. Mirror of anhui-clique /ledger/5, which lists Anhui with Shaanxi, Gansu and Hunan: the page does not say that those three were annexed by Zhili, and this dossier takes only Anhui. [ea-08-x repair 2026-10-25: added; the 1925-1926 shape held Anhui with no gain.]
March 1924: Fujian. 'Sun Chuanfang gained Fujian in March 1924.' The Anhui clique page has Li Houji governing Fujian 1914-1923 and the province 'reliant on the Anhui Clique'.
3 September 1924: the Jiangsu-Zhejiang War. 'On 3 September, his forces attacked the Anhui forces in Zhejiang and Shanghai.'

region.text: Tangshan, Lutai and Luanzhou on the Shanhaiguan-Tianjin line

ledger.note: 15 September 1924: the Second Zhili-Fengtian War begins (infobox 'September 15, 1924 - November 3, 1924').
12 October 1924: the war 'ended on 12 October 1924 with an Anhui defeat'.

October 1924: Zhejiang and Shanghai are Zhili's after the Jiangsu-Zhejiang War (Anhui defeat on 12 October 1924); Lu Yongxiang's Zhejiang army and He Fenglin's Shanghai were the Anhui clique's (Anhui clique page).

22 October 1924: Feng Yuxiang's Beijing Coup takes the capital from the Zhili clique. The Second Zhili-Fengtian War page dates the coup 'October 22' (the Zhili and Feng Yuxiang pages say 23 October); Cao Kun was toppled ('Feng occupied Beijing and forced Cao to resign', Cao Kun page, 2026-10-25). Mirror of guominjun /ledger/0. [ea-08-x repair 2026-10-25: split out of the single November 1924 loss, as the reviewer asked, because guominjun /ledger/0 takes Beijing in October.]

region.text: Tangshan, Lutai, Luanzhou and the line to Tianjin

ledger.note: 3 November 1924: the Second Zhili-Fengtian War ends; Wu Peifu left Tianjin by sea. It 'ended in defeat for Zhili when Zhang Zuolin paid Feng Yuxiang to switch sides'; 'Feng captured Beijing for the Fengtian clique on 23 October 1924' (Zhili page; the Second Zhili-Fengtian page says 22 October).

November 1924 (bridging): the war ends with 'a Zhili loss of all of its northern provinces to Zhang Zuolin and Feng Yuxiang's Guominjun'; the page does not name Chahar or Suiyuan. The Guominjun page says the Guominjun 'had control of much of Northwestern China, including Shaanxi, Chahar and Suiyuan' without a date, so the transfer of the two special districts to the Guominjun is a reading. Mirror of guominjun's gain of Chahar and Suiyuan (guominjun ledger, 1924-11). [ea-08-x repair 2026-10-25: split out of the single November 1924 loss.]

November 1924: Zhili's north falls. The page: 'a Zhili loss of all of its northern provinces to Zhang Zuolin and Feng Yuxiang's Guominjun'; the page does not split the shares, so Hebei and Tianjin to Fengtian is a reading (the Fengtian dossier gains them, shared with the Guominjun, in November 1924). Beijing (to the Guominjun, October), Chahar and Suiyuan (to the Guominjun) and Rehe (to Fengtian) are separate events. [ea-08-x repair 2026-10-25: the single loss of all the north to fengtian-clique was split into five events as the reviewer asked, because guominjun /ledger/0 takes Beijing and the Guominjun page gives it Chahar and Suiyuan.]

November 1924 (bridging): Rehe goes with the rest of Zhili's north, to Fengtian by the reviewer's split. The Second Zhili-Fengtian War page names Rehe only as a battlefront and the Rehe Province page (opened 2026-10-25) is silent on 1924; confidence 1. Mirror of the fengtian-clique gain of Rehe (1924-11). [ea-08-x repair 2026-10-25: added; before it, Rehe was lost to no one.]

1925 (bridging): the Northern Expedition page lists 'Wu Peifu: Held northern Hunan, Hubei, and Henan in 1926'; how and when Wu came to hold northern Hunan is not on the pages opened, and 'nobody' stands for the several Hunan authorities. [ea-08-x repair 2026-10-25, thin item: the Wu Peifu page (opened) is silent on Hunan: it says only 'Wu maintained a power base in Hubei and Henan in central China' and that he was forced 'to withdraw to Zhengzhou in Henan' in 1927; how Wu came to hold northern Hunan, and whether the region is whole or northern Hunan, stays unsettled, so confidence stays 1 and the region stays the Northern Expedition page's 'northern Hunan'.]

By August 1925: Jiangsu and Anhui are the Fengtian Army's. Zhang Zuolin page (re-read 2026-10-25): 'By August 1925, the Fengtian Army controlled four large provinces within the Great Wall' (Zhili, Shandong, Jiangsu, Anhui); 'one unit even marched as far south as the city of Shanghai'. The page gives no earlier date (the Second Zhili-Fengtian War page: 'Fighting continued well into 1925 as part of the Jiangsu-Zhejiang War when a joint Anhui-Fengtian expedition briefly retook Jiangsu and Shanghai in January', a brief hold that this dossier does not draw), so the month is the page's bound. Mirror of fengtian-clique /ledger/9. [ea-08-x repair 2026-10-25: added at the reviewer's request; the first version held both provinces through 1925-1926.]

region.text: Jiangsu and Anhui back under Sun Chuanfang

ledger.note: 25 November 1925: Sun Chuanfang is again master of Jiangsu. Sun Chuanfang page (re-read 2026-10-25): he 'set up headquarters in Nanjing as military governor of Jiangsu' on 25 November 1925, after a fall-1925 counterattack that 'drove Zhang Zongchang and his forces out of the Chinese districts of Shanghai', and 'expanded his rule to include all of Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Anhui and Jiangxi'; Anhui is not dated separately. The Anti-Fengtian War page (the one the review pointed to) is the Guominjun's war of November 1925 - April 1926 and says nothing of the two provinces. Mirror of fengtian-clique /ledger/10. [ea-08-x repair 2026-10-25: added.]
22 August 1926: Hunan falls. 'Changsha fell to the KMT on 11 July 1926, and Hunan was fully under KMT control after Yuezhou fell on 22 August 1926.'
10 October 1926: Wuchang surrenders. 'Wu Peifu's remaining forces at Wuchang surrendered on 10 October 1926, completing the NRA's conquest of Hubei province.'
9 November 1926: the NRA 'by 9 November 1926, retook control of Nanchang'; Jiangxi is Sun Chuanfang's in the page's 1926 snapshot.
9 December 1926: 'He Yingqin's forces entered Fuzhou on 9 December 1926.'
By 23 February 1927: 'Zhejiang was under complete KMT control by 23 February 1927.'
22 March 1927: 'on 22 March 1927, Bai's forces marched into Shanghai victorious.'

28 May 1927: the Guominjun takes Luoyang and, with it, Henan. Northern Expedition page (re-read 2026-10-25): 'On 28 May, Li took Suzhou, while the Guominjun took Luoyang, forcing Zhang Zongchang to withdraw his forces to Shandong, and Zhang Xueliang to fall back north of the Yellow River'; 'Following Xueliang's retreat, Feng Yuxiang moved east from Luoyang to Zhengzhou'. Henan was Wu Peifu's in 1926, with Fengtian reinforcements 'in support of Wu Peifu' from about February 1927 and the Wuhan army's Tang Shengzhi also attacking in May, so Henan as a whole to the Guominjun is a reading (confidence 2); Wu retreated into Sichuan about June 1927 after 'withdraw[ing] to Zhengzhou'. Mirror of the Guominjun's Henan gain (guominjun ledger, 1927-5). [ea-08-x repair 2026-10-25: added; Henan left the 1927 shape with no event.]

Late August 1927: the last Zhili army falls. Sun Chuanfang 'retreated to Nanjing and was defeated at Longtan in late August 1927'; 'The Zhili clique was the only warlord faction to be destroyed as a result of the Northern Expedition' (Zhili page; its infobox says 'Active: 1920-1928'). Henan's loss is not dated on the pages.

wars.name: Zhili-Anhui War
wars.outcome: Zhili and Fengtian victory: the Anhui clique was destroyed and Duan Qirui resigned on 19 July 1920.
wars.note: 14-23 July 1920; fought at Zhuozhou, Gaobeidian, Langfang and Nanyuan.

wars.name: First Zhili-Fengtian War
wars.outcome: Zhili victory; Fengtian retreated to Manchuria and Shanhaiguan became the border.

wars.name: First Jiangsu-Zhejiang War
wars.outcome: Zhili victory: Zhejiang and Shanghai taken from the Anhui clique; the war 'ended on 12 October 1924 with an Anhui defeat'.

wars.name: Second Zhili-Fengtian War
wars.outcome: Zhili defeat: Feng Yuxiang's coup and the Fengtian advance cost Zhili all its northern provinces.

wars.name: Anti-Fengtian War

zones.text: the Beijing-Tianjin plain: Tianjin seized by Feng Yuxiang in December 1925, Beijing occupied by Zhang Xueliang's army in April 1926, with Wu's troops arriving later

wars.outcome: Fengtian and Zhili victory (infobox): the Guominjun was driven from Tianjin and Beijing; 'Zhang and Wu jointly occupied Beijing'. Zhili's part was Wu Peifu's, in the allied army of 1926; no land of the Zhili clique's own changed hands in the war on the page.
wars.note: Infobox November 1925 - April 1926. Sun Chuanfang is described as Zhili-affiliated but is not a listed belligerent. [ea-08-x repair 2026-10-25: added at the reviewer's request.]

wars.name: Northern Expedition
wars.outcome: Kuomintang victory: Hunan (22 August 1926), Hubei (10 October), Jiangxi (9 November), Fuzhou (9 December), Zhejiang (23 February 1927), Shanghai (22 March) and Sun Chuanfang's defeat at Longtan in late August 1927.
wars.note: The Zhili clique was destroyed by it. [ea-08-x repair 2026-10-25: belligerents are slugs now; 'Sun Chuanfang' and 'Wu Peifu' were name strings and belong to zhili-clique; the Guominjun took Henan on 28 May 1927 (loss event 1927-5) and Fengtian forces fought in Henan and Shandong.]

certainty.note: Provincial control by garrison commanders; the pages give no boundaries other than whole provinces, and the clique's grip on each province changed with the wars.

notes:
Written by ea-08-x on 2026-10-25 from six pages; Cliopatria has no Zhili row (the Republic of China row, ea-08-c, draws all of China as one state). Settled: the 1920 founding, the 1922 war, the Fujian, Zhejiang and Shanghai gains of 1924, the November 1924 loss of the north, and the dated 1926-1927 falls. The dossier ends in August 1927 (Sun's defeat at Longtan on the Northern Expedition page); the Zhili page's infobox says 'Active: 1920-1928'.

Not settled: (1) the formation of the clique before 1920 (the page gives no date); (2) the undated 'at its height' control of Jiangsu, Jiangxi and Hubei and the 1922 'consolidation' of Henan (confidence 1); (3) how Wu Peifu came to hold northern Hunan (confidence 1, counterpart 'nobody'); (4) what happened to Henan (the Northern Expedition page says only that Wu held it in 1926 and gives no loss date); (5) the split of the November 1924 north between Fengtian and the Guominjun, and whether Rehe, Chahar and Suiyuan went to the latter (the Guominjun page says it controlled Chahar and Suiyuan without a date); (6) Beijing's coup date (22 October on the Second Zhili-Fengtian page, 23 October on the Zhili page); (7) Anhui's holder before Sun Chuanfang and the Sichuan, Shaanxi and Hunan connections (not on the pages). The capitals are seats of the governments or commanders the pages name, not named capitals of the clique. Counterparts without dossiers: Sun Chuanfang's Five Provinces Alliance (1925-1927). Gazetteer: all names resolved except the Shanhaiguan corridor, a polygon.

[ea-08-x repair 2026-10-25, after the adversarial review (verdict fail)] (1) Anhui: added a gain from anhui-clique 'by the summer of 1924' (confidence 1, Anhui clique page: 'all their provinces were eventually annexed'); that page does not say Shaanxi, Gansu or Hunan were annexed by Zhili, which anhui-clique /ledger/5 lists, so only Anhui is mirrored here. (2) Jiangsu and Anhui: a loss to fengtian-clique in August 1925 (Zhang Zuolin page: four provinces 'by August 1925') and a return in November 1925 (Sun Chuanfang page: Nanjing headquarters on 25 November 1925). I did not use the Anti-Fengtian War page for the return, as the review suggested: the page is the Guominjun's war of November 1925 - April 1926 and does not mention Jiangsu, Anhui or Sun's recovery. The Anti-Fengtian War is added to the wars. (3) The November 1924 loss is split into five events as the reviewer asked: Beijing to the Guominjun (1924-10, 22 October on the war page), Chahar and Suiyuan to the Guominjun (1924-11, confidence 1: the Guominjun page gives them undated), Hebei and Tianjin to Fengtian (confidence 2) and Rehe to Fengtian (confidence 1: the Rehe Province page, opened, names no holder). (4) Henan: a loss to guominjun on 28 May 1927 (Luoyang), confidence 2: the Northern Expedition page shows Fengtian and Wuhan forces in Henan in the same weeks, so the counterpart is the reviewer's reading as much as the page's. (5) Not settled: the dates of Zhili's holdings of Henan, Jiangsu, Jiangxi and Hubei (the Cao Kun page, opened, lists no provinces and no years); how Wu Peifu came to hold Hunan (the Wu Peifu page is silent on Hunan); Shanghai in January-fall 1925 (the Sun Chuanfang page says Sun's fall-1925 counterattack drove Zhang Zongchang out of Shanghai's Chinese districts, which would mean Shanghai was lost to Fengtian-aligned troops too; no page dates it, and Shanghai is kept in the 1925 shape).
